findings.title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the sqlExpressions feature flag entirely
findings.body: The new enableSqlExpressions() unconditionally returns false: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false on every path, so even operators who explicitly enable the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle will get the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" for every SQL expression query. If hard-disabling is the intent of this security fix, the convoluted always-false logic is misleading — a plain `return false` (or removing the feature flag check and the flag reference) would be honest about the behavior. As written, the feature flag documentation (which this PR explicitly says it is leaving untouched) tells users a toggle exists that silently does nothing, and the dead negation invites a future edit to mistakenly re-enable the vulnerable code path by 'fixing' what looks like a bug.
